newsitem.title: USA: Stricken Finnish tourist robbed by phony Samaritan.
newsitem.headline: Stricken Finnish tourist robbed by phony Samaritan.

text.p: Police have arrested a suspect who posed as a Good Samaritan to rob an elderly Finnish tourist who was suffering a heart attack on a Manhattan street.

The elderly tourist, Laila Simola, arrived in New York from Helsinki on Thursday for a two-week stay with her daughter, Lisa Simola, a freelance journalist. On Friday the woman took her mother sightseeing in the East Village area of Manhattan when the elder Simola clutched her heart and collapsed to the pavement.
As the daughter went to seek assistance, a woman rushed to the elderly Simola and knelt to hold the hand of the unconscious Finnish visitor.
According to police, the woman stole an heirloom, 1.5 carat diamond ring off of the elder Simola's finger.

Police identified the suspect as Donna Parker, 38. She has been charged with grand larceny and criminal possession of stolen property. Parker has a history of several petty larceny arrests, a police spokesman said.
The ring had not been recovered and police were searching for an accomplice who they said may have sold the ring.
Simola was in stable condition in a hospital's coronary care unit.
